question: Why does Chapter 10 measure 64 req/s and Chapter 8 48 req/s for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct BF16 on an H100 80GB with the same objectives (TTFT 500 ms, TPOT 50 ms)?
answer: Prompt reuse with prefix caching. Chapter 10's benchmark draws its requests from 500 HotpotQA prompts with prefix caching on; the 500 prompts (about 342,000 tokens) fit in the 454,096-token KV cache, so after the first use 98.8% of prompt tokens come from the cache and prefill is almost skipped: capacity is at least 80 req/s (cell D). The same prompts without caching reach only 32 req/s (cell C), below Chapter 8's 48, because they are longer (median 689 tokens against 510). Chapter 8's 1,000 prompts (about 505,000 tokens) do not fit in the KV cache, so with caching on they hit only 0.9-20% of prompt tokens and capacity stays at 48 (cell B = cell A). The capacity rules agree in every cell; repeats matter only at cell C's 40 req/s edge (2 of 3 repeats fail).
platform: GPU cluster, 1 x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (SXM, 700 W), one Slurm job

env.host_cpu: not recorded in this job (earlier runs on this cluster's H100 nodes: Intel Xeon Platinum 8468)
env.kv_cache_tokens: 454,096 (452,240 on one of the seven server starts), from the vLLM startup log

method.load_generator: chapter08/loadgen.py one_request() (completions endpoint, temperature 0, ignore_eos, 128 output tokens, special tokens streamed) on its open-loop Poisson schedule; prompts sent in order from a per-run offset; every per-request record kept (chapter10/capacity_ablation.py)
method.repeats: 3 per cell, fresh server each; 60 s warm-up at 32 req/s; repeat 1 sweeps every rate in ascending order, repeats 2 and 3 run repeat 1's knee rate and its neighbours in rotated orders
method.chapter8_rule: per run: requests with TTFT <= 500 ms and TPOT <= 50 ms over requests sent (failures count), TPOT = (e2e - TTFT)/(tokens - 1); capacity = highest rate with >= 90% in every repeat
method.chapter10_rule: serve_bench.sweep(): the same share with TPOT = (end - first chunk)/(stream lines - 1), the chat stream adding a role and a finish line; capacity = highest rate with >= 90% in one run (repeat 1)
method.prefix_hit_rate: delta of vllm:prefix_cache_hits over vllm:prefix_cache_queries (tokens) during each run
method.reused_prompt_share: share of a run's requests whose prompt had already been sent to the same server (1.0 everywhere: the warm-up covers the whole pool)

ch8.output_tokens: 128 for every request (ignore_eos), as in both chapters

hotpot.output_tokens: 128 for every request (ignore_eos), as in both chapters

prompts.note: token counts with the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct tokenizer, add_special_tokens=True (as the completions endpoint tokenizes); HotpotQA prompts rendered with the chat template, leading BOS removed

differences_found: prompts: Chapter 8 prompts_single.jsonl (1,000, median 510 tokens) vs Chapter 10 HotpotQA eval.jsonl[:500] with the chat template (median 689)
prefix caching: off in Chapter 8, on in Chapter 10
prompt choice: Chapter 8 cycles through the prompts in order; Chapter 10 picks uniformly at random with replacement, the same seed at every rate
endpoint and client: Chapter 8 /v1/completions with aiohttp; Chapter 10 /v1/chat/completions with httpx (max 2,000 connections)
TPOT: Chapter 8 divides by completion tokens (skip_special_tokens off); Chapter 10 by stream lines (special tokens skipped)
max-model-len: 2,048 in Chapter 8's sweep, 4,096 in Chapter 10
duration: Chapter 8 knee runs 30 s of arrivals (rate x 30 requests), Chapter 10 60 s
warm-up and repeats: Chapter 8 three repeats with a 60 s warm-up; Chapter 10 one run after 20 single requests
rate grid: Chapter 8's knee runs 24, 32, 48, 64; Chapter 10's sweep 4 to 192 with 64 then 80, so both published capacities are lower bounds of their brackets (Ch 8: 48 <= c < 64; Ch 10: 64 <= c < 80)
platform: Modal, vLLM 0.32.0, driver 610.57.04 (Chapter 8) vs this cluster, vLLM 0.33.0, driver 590.48.01 (Chapter 10)

capacity_req_s.note: 80 req/s is the highest rate tested: every D run passed, so the capacity is at least 80

not_run: cell D10 (HotpotQA, caching on, Chapter 10's random prompt order): skipped by the job's deadline guard
raw_files: raw logs and per-request records kept with the book sources (not in this repository)
